It is rare to find lexical minimal pairs differentiated by tone alone. ... sweep_summary: masa1299 Masaaba (Lumasaaba/Lugisu, Bantu JE31) is not in the catalog. The single Glottolog stress/accent-title item, Philippson 1991 (Tons et accent dans les langues bantu d'Afrique Orientale), was already held by the project from an earlier reading of this reading (downloaded from ddl.cnrs.fr; copied into the masa1299 directory) and was read in full where it treats Masaaba: pp. 257-258 derive Masaaba verb forms with an autosegmental 'accentual' mark that takes a BH tone melody and repeats on all non-final theme moras, fn. 2 p. 258 says Meeussen's rule does not apply in Masaaba, p. 413 states 'en bukusu, comme en masaaba, la mélodie accentuelle est de forme BH', and the annex table (p. 502) tabulates group VII only through Bukusu ('système accentuel avec mélodie *BH'; penultimate-syllable status 'néant'). 'Accent' there is a tone mark, not stress: the thesis contains no word-stress statement for Masaaba (relevance: prosody-but-not-word-stress; no-catalog-record). Brown 1971 (Edinburgh PhD, held by the project, re-read) likewise says Lumasaaba is a grammatical-tone language (two tones + downstep) and is silent on stress. No first-hand word-stress statement for Masaaba was read, so no new stress statement was found. IV 'Characteristics of the Gisu group' (archive.org copy access-restricted, Routledge 403; medium priority), Siertsema 1968 Lingua orthography paper (paywalled; low), and de Blois 1975 appendix 5 on Masaaba (not online; low); Purvis 1907 grammar (HathiTrust/Google Books, both could not be reached by automated download) remains the highest-priority unopened source. all probe outputs and an addendum are filed under and there.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The source treats Lumasaaba as a two-tone (H/L, plus probable downstep) language with mainly grammatical tone and makes no statement about word stress at all. The only word-level prominence generalisation is tonal: for nouns said in isolation (Buhugu dialect) the prefix(es) carry low tone, the first stem syllable high tone and the last stem syllable low tone; a long first stem vowel carries a falling tone.
new_statements.exceptions: Monosyllabic stems with a preceding glide take a fall; monosyllabic stems without a glide have an unstable isolation pattern (L-prefix + H-stem or H-prefix + L-stem); two prefixes coalesced into one long vowel are always high in isolation; considerable inter-token and inter-dialect variation in tone patterns (e.g. Buhugu vs Buwalasi 'a fly'); downdrift/automatic downstep said not to occur.
new_statements.domain_note: Nouns uttered in isolation, Buhugu (Central Bugisu) dialect; informal sketch of 'probabilities of realisation', not a formal tone analysis; tone left unmarked in the rest of the description.
new_statements.identity_note: Brown 1971/1972 describe Lumasaaba as spoken in Bugisu (Mbale area, Uganda), i.e. the Ugandan Masaaba/Gisu varieties of masa1299, with six main dialects; the tone sketch quoted is explicitly for the Buhugu dialect (Central Bugisu). Kenyan Bukusu (buku1249), sometimes grouped with Masaba by Guthrie, is not covered. Purvis 1907 describes the Busoba (Central) variety.

sources.quote: Lumasaaba is a tone language, like most East African Bantu languages, in which tone is used primarily for making grammatical rather than lexical distinctions. It is rare to find lexical minimal pairs differentiated by tone alone. ... Most nouns in isolation are realised with low tone on the prefix(es), high tone on the first syllable of the stem and low tone on the last syllable of the stem ... It seems likely that an adequate account of the tonal phenomena in Lumasaaba could be made in terms of two tones, one high and one low, and a feature of downstep
sources.note: First-hand phonology (Buhugu dialect, fieldwork + Edinburgh informant): Lumasaaba is a grammatical-tone language, two tones plus downstep; a long stem-initial vowel carries a falling tone. The word 'stress' occurs three times in the thesis, none about Lumasaaba; no word-stress statement anywhere. Silent on stress.
